## Description

This page studies numerical approximation of a rectangular double integral with the
composite 2D Trapezoidal and 2D Simpson rules. Examples 1–6 of the archived module use

$$
I = \int_0^1 \int_0^1 8e^{-x^2-y^4}\,dy\,dx,
$$

with surface $z=8e^{-x^2-y^4}$ over $R=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 1,\ 0\le y\le 1\}$.

For a tensor-product grid, the 2D Trapezoidal rule applies endpoint/interior weights
along each axis and sums weighted samples:

$$
I_{T} \approx hk\sum_{i=0}^{m}\sum_{j=0}^{n} w_i w_j f(x_i,y_j),
\qquad
w_0=w_m=\tfrac{1}{2},\ w_i=1\ (1\le i\le m-1),
$$

and the 2D Simpson rule uses the product Simpson weights:

$$
I_{S} \approx \frac{hk}{9}\sum_{i=0}^{m}\sum_{j=0}^{n} a_i a_j f(x_i,y_j),
\qquad
a_0=a_m=1,\ a_i=4\ \text{(odd } i\text{)},\ a_i=2\ \text{(even } i,\ 0<i<m\text{)}.
$$

Here the rectangle $[a,b]\times[c,d]$ is divided into $m$ panels of width $h=(b-a)/m$
in $x$ and $n$ panels of width $k=(d-c)/n$ in $y$, with nodes $x_i=a+ih$ and
$y_j=c+jk$; the weights $w_j$ and $a_j$ are defined in the same way with $n$ in place
of $m$. For Simpson's rule $m$ and $n$ must be even.

## Animations

Each animation shows full-domain mesh refinement on $[0,1]\times[0,1]$ for
$f(x,y)=8e^{-x^2-y^4}$, using the archived benchmark
$I\approx 5.04756680717$.

Julia source scripts that generated these animations are linked under each case.

The archived snapshot is incomplete for some intermediate image IDs, so these
animations are reconstructed from the available formula and checkpoint assets.
The module's Example 7, which applies the composite Simpson's rule to a double integral
whose inner limits of integration are functions of $x$ (a non-rectangular region), is
not animated here.

### Case 1 - 2D Trapezoidal Rule, $f(x,y)=8e^{-x^2-y^4}$

**Behavior:** The coarse-to-fine tensor grid updates over the whole square each frame.
The approximation converges toward the archived reference value, with visible
second-order error decay under refinement. The black lines join the sample nodes with
straight segments: they are the grid lines of the piecewise-bilinear interpolant,
whose integral is the trapezoidal value $I_T$.

[Julia source](trapezoidal2daa.jl)

![2D Trapezoidal animation: coloured surface of f over [0,1]x[0,1] with straight black grid lines through the sample nodes (the bilinear interpolant), full-grid refinement from 2x2 to 20x20, and convergence to the archived benchmark integral](trapezoidal2daa.gif)

### Case 2 - 2D Simpson Rule, $f(x,y)=8e^{-x^2-y^4}$

**Behavior:** Simpson tensor-product weights are recomputed on each refined mesh.
Compared with trapezoidal refinement, the Simpson estimate reaches high accuracy
with fewer refinements. The black curves are the quadratics through the sample nodes
over each pair of panels along every grid line: the grid lines of the
piecewise-biquadratic interpolant (one patch per 2x2 block of panels), whose integral
is the Simpson value $I_S$. On the 2x2 mesh they differ from the trapezoidal straight
lines by up to 0.51 in $z$.

[Julia source](simpson2daa.jl)

![2D Simpson animation: coloured surface of f over [0,1]x[0,1] with black piecewise-quadratic grid curves through the sample nodes (the biquadratic interpolant), tensor-product Simpson refinement from 2x2 to 20x20, and convergence toward the archived benchmark integral](simpson2daa.gif)
